title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Entry Requirements and Proposal Validity by Tier
content:
## Proposal desk sheet

Before a tier of the Preventive Maintenance Agreements is proposed for a building, the estimating desk reads the tier's entry figures from this sheet: the minimum count of covered units, the maximum age of any unit at proposal, whether a completed pre-agreement inspection is required, the fee for that inspection, and how long the proposal stays open for signature.

| Tier | Minimum number of covered units on the schedule | Maximum age of any covered unit at proposal, from install date (calendar months; 1200 means no age limit) | Completed pre-agreement inspection work order required before proposal | Pre-agreement inspection fee, credited against the first installment if the agreement activates (USD) | Calendar days the proposal remains open for signature |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter & Belt Service Plan | 4 | 1200 | no | 0 | 30 |
| Inspection Agreement | 2 | 1200 | no | 0 | 30 |
| Preventive Maintenance Agreement | 2 | 1200 | no | 0 | 45 |
| Labor Coverage Agreement | 2 | 240 | yes | 450 | 45 |
| Full Coverage Agreement | 2 | 180 | yes | 650 | 45 |
| Comprehensive Performance Agreement | 6 | 120 | yes | 950 | 60 |

### Sheet notes

- An age figure of 1200 months means the tier sets no age limit; the three lower tiers set none. The Labor Coverage Agreement limits unit age to 240 months, the Full Coverage Agreement to 180 months and the Comprehensive Performance Agreement to 120 months.
- The pre-agreement inspection is required, and its fee published, only at the three upper tiers: 450 USD, 650 USD and 950 USD respectively. Where the tier requires no inspection the fee is 0.
- The Filter & Belt Service Plan needs at least 4 covered units and the Comprehensive Performance Agreement at least 6; every other tier needs at least 2.
- Proposal validity is 30 calendar days at the two entry tiers, 45 at the three middle tiers and 60 at the Comprehensive Performance Agreement.
